why: Issue #930's second half: the badge has NO `opacity: 0` in its own rule -- it rests invisible because `animation: ... both` holds a keyframe set opening at `opacity: 0`, which is how all three stock-cue arms do it and why a population derived from base rules alone would miss them. NOT A CLOSED GAP, and worth stating plainly: this mutation was already killed before issue #930 by the arms' own case in `hud.css: the stock-loss cue arms (issue #230)`, and it still fails that one too. What the derived rule adds here is a SECOND, general guard -- the #230 case is arm-specific and a fourth arm added tomorrow joins the derived population automatically. The gap this issue actually closed is `hud-css-cancels-the-damage-vignette`, which the old suite did not catch at all.
killedBy: hud.css: every animation answers to the resolved motion policy (issue #631) never answers an animation by cancelling a cue that rests invisible
hud.css: the stock-loss cue arms (issue #230) gives every cue a reduced-motion form, keyed off the resolved policy class
